# @zakkster/lite-watch-ex

> Extended watcher utilities for `@zakkster/lite-signal`. One-shot watchers
> with auto-dispose, predicate-gated watchers, Vue-style `watchEffect`. Zero
> JS-heap allocations per source change in steady state. Re-exports the core
> `watch` / `when` / `whenAsync`. ESM-only, MIT licensed, ~1 KB min+gz.

Three new exports plus three re-exports. All three new ones build on
lite-signal's `effect` + `untrack` + `onCleanup`. One-shots truly self-dispose
on fire -- the effect node returns to lite-signal's pool, not merely silenced
by a flag.

## Core API

- **`watchOnce(source, callback, options?)`** -- fire once on the first
  non-equal change (or immediately, if `options.immediate === true`), then
  self-dispose.
- **`watchUntil(source, predicate, callback)`** -- fire once when
  `predicate(newValue)` first passes on a changed value (or initially if
  already truthy), then self-dispose.
- **`watchEffect(callback)`** -- `effect()` with `onCleanup` pre-injected as
  a callback argument. Vue-style ergonomic; identical alloc profile to
  plain `effect()`.

- **`watchPrevious(source, callback, options?)`** (1.1) -- rolling history;
  callback gets `(current, history, stop)` with the previous `depth` values
  (default 1), newest-first, in a reused buffer. `copy` for a fresh array.
- **`watchChanged(source, predicate, callback, options?)`** (1.1) -- ongoing
  watcher gated by a `(new, old)` predicate; fires on every passing change.
- **`pausableWatch(source, callback, options?)`** (1.1) -- pausable ongoing
  watcher; returns `{ stop, pause, resume, isPaused }`. `fireOnResume` for a
  single catch-up on resume.
- **`watchMany(sources, callback, options?)`** (1.1) -- fixed tuple of sources;
  fires with `(values, oldValues, changedIndex, stop)`. Reused buffers; `copy`
  for fresh arrays.

## Re-exports

- **`watch`** -- ongoing watcher with `(next, prev, stop)` from lite-signal.
- **`when`** -- fire once when predicate first truthy, no old/new pair.
- **`whenAsync`** -- Promise variant of `when`. (!) allocates per call.

Importing from `@zakkster/lite-watch-ex` or `@zakkster/lite-signal` resolves
to the same function -- the re-export is for ergonomic convenience.

## Architecture invariants

- **Hoisted untrack body**: the `untrack(untrackedFire)` call passes a closure
  allocated ONCE at registration. Shared state (currentNewValue, oldValue,
  fired) lives in closure-scoped `let` bindings. Declaring `untrack(() => {...})`
  inline inside the effect body would allocate a fresh closure per fire -- the
  pattern lite-signal's `Watch.js` "ZERO-GC HOT PATH" comment warns against.
  This package follows that warning.
- **Self-dispose from inside the effect**: when a one-shot fires, the
  registered stop function is called from within the effect body. Signal.js's
  effect dispose is idempotent and safe to call from within the executing
  effect (verified at Signal.js:746-784) -- the node is destroyed and returns
  to the pool. Subsequent source changes don't reach the watcher.
- **Late-binding stop wrapper**: `stop` is a closure that resolves `stopFn`
  lazily, with a `wantsStopEarly` flag for the case where the user calls
  `stop()` synchronously inside an immediate-mode callback before `effect()`
  has returned. Mirror of the pattern in lite-signal's `when()`.
- **Intent guard via `Object.is`**: `NaN`-to-`NaN` is a no-op. `+0`/`-0`
  distinct. Same equality contract as the rest of lite-signal.
- **Callback reads are untracked**: callback body runs inside `untrack`, so
  side-effect reads don't accidentally subscribe the watcher to other signals.

## Performance characteristics

- `watchOnce`/`watchUntil` per source change in steady state: O(1), zero
  JS-heap alloc. Hot path is read source -> intent compare -> conditional
  predicate eval -> optional callback + dispose.
- `watchEffect` per source change: same as plain `effect()` from lite-signal.
- Registration: one effect node + links from lite-signal's pools, plus 3
  closures (effect body, untrackedFire body, stop wrapper) for one-shots, or
  1 closure for `watchEffect`. All reused for the life of the instance.
- Self-dispose: O(1) -- single flag flip + lite-signal's node release.

## When to use

- Initialization tied to a state transition: `watchOnce` (immediate or trailing).
- Threshold alerts that should fire once and stop: `watchUntil`.
- Reactive bodies with per-run teardown: `watchEffect` with `onCleanup`.
- Vue / Solid migrations: `watchEffect` reads identically to the Vue version.

## When NOT to use

- Continuous observation: use `watch` (from lite-signal). One-shots are exactly
  one-shot.
- Truthiness gates without needing old/new pair: use `when` -- smaller surface.
- Async control flow inside a render loop: `whenAsync` allocates a Promise per
  call. Use `when` with a callback instead.

## API summary

```ts
function watchOnce<T>(
    source: () => T,
    callback: (newValue: T, oldValue: T | undefined) => void,
    options?: { immediate?: boolean }
): () => void;

function watchUntil<T>(
    source: () => T,
    predicate: (value: T) => unknown,
    callback: (newValue: T, oldValue: T | undefined) => void
): () => void;

function watchEffect(
    callback: (onCleanup: (fn: () => void) => void) => void
): () => void;

function watchPrevious<T>(
    source: () => T,
    callback: (current: T, history: Array<T | undefined>, stop: () => void) => void,
    options?: { depth?: number; immediate?: boolean; copy?: boolean }
): () => void;

function watchChanged<T>(
    source: () => T,
    predicate: (newValue: T, oldValue: T | undefined) => unknown,
    callback: (newValue: T, oldValue: T | undefined, stop: () => void) => void,
    options?: { immediate?: boolean }
): () => void;

function pausableWatch<T>(
    source: () => T,
    callback: (newValue: T, oldValue: T | undefined, stop: () => void) => void,
    options?: { immediate?: boolean; fireOnResume?: boolean }
): { stop: () => void; pause: () => void; resume: () => void; readonly isPaused: boolean };

function watchMany<T>(
    sources: Array<() => T>,
    callback: (values: T[], oldValues: T[], changedIndex: number, stop: () => void) => void,
    options?: { immediate?: boolean; copy?: boolean }
): () => void;

// Re-exports -- see @zakkster/lite-signal
function watch<T>(...): () => void;
function when(...): () => void;
function whenAsync(...): Promise<void>;
```

## Idioms

```js
// One-shot trailing
const status = signal("loading");
watchOnce(status, (next) => initialize(next));

// One-shot immediate
watchOnce(currentUser, (u) => greet(u), { immediate: true });

// Predicate-gated one-shot
watchUntil(() => player.health(), (h) => h <= 25, (h) => hud.warn(h));

// Vue-style watchEffect with cleanup
watchEffect((onCleanup) => {
    const id = requestAnimationFrame(() => render());
    onCleanup(() => cancelAnimationFrame(id));
});
```

## File layout

- `WatchEx.js`              -- implementations + JSDoc + re-exports.
- `index.js`                -- barrel re-export of all six functions.
- `index.d.ts`              -- TypeScript declarations.
- `test/watchEx.test.mjs`   -- node:test behavior + heap-delta suite (not published).

## Install

```bash
npm install @zakkster/lite-watch-ex @zakkster/lite-signal
```

`@zakkster/lite-signal` is a peer dependency.
